questions.q: Jim and Ron ___ for hours about the political situation
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a completed action in the past ('for hours'), so the simple past tense 'talked' is correct.

questions.q: Chinese is ___ language to read.
questions.explanation: We use the superlative 'the most difficult' when describing the highest degree of a quality. The definite article 'the' is required with superlatives.

questions.q: We ___ our sandwiches and went back to work.
questions.explanation: 'Ate' is the simple past tense of 'eat', which is required here because the sentence describes a completed past action (coordinated with 'went back').

questions.q: "Sorry." "___ worry."
questions.explanation: 'Don't worry' is the standard English response to an apology, using the imperative negative form.

questions.q: I am ___ than my brother.
questions.explanation: When comparing two people, the comparative form 'more intelligent' is used, not the superlative.

questions.q: Would you like ___ a drink?
questions.explanation: 'Would you like' is followed by the infinitive with 'to', so 'to have' is correct.

questions.q: I'll ___ 2 seats at the theater for tomorrow night.
questions.explanation: After the modal verb 'will', the base form of the verb (bare infinitive) is used: 'I'll book'.

questions.q: House prices ___ much higher last year than today.
questions.explanation: 'House prices' is a plural subject, and the sentence refers to last year (past), so 'were' is the correct past tense plural form of 'to be'.

questions.q: I ___ the piano.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs like 'can' are always followed by the base form of the verb (bare infinitive), so 'can play' is correct.

questions.q: That's my ___ book on the table.
questions.explanation: To show possession, we use the possessive apostrophe: 'friend's' means the book belongs to the friend.

questions.q: Is ___ bus over there ours?
questions.explanation: 'Bus' is singular and located 'over there' (at a distance), so the singular distant demonstrative 'that' is correct.

questions.q: The bank's ___ the left. Next to the police station.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition for directions is 'on the left' (or 'on the right').

questions.q: ___ was very tired.
questions.explanation: 'She' is the only singular third-person subject pronoun among the options that correctly pairs with the singular verb 'was'.

questions.q: ___ boss gives us our pay every week in a small brown envelope.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun is needed to modify the noun 'boss'. 'Our' is the correct possessive adjective form here.

questions.q: You're ___ than I am!
questions.explanation: The structure '___er/more ___ than' requires the comparative form. 'More selfish' is the correct comparative of 'selfish'.

questions.q: The door isn't locked. ___ into the office.
questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence giving a suggestion or instruction. The base form 'Go' is used for imperatives.

questions.q: Our opinions change ___ we get older.
questions.explanation: 'As' is used to express two things happening simultaneously or progressively together: 'as we get older' means 'at the same time / in proportion to getting older'.

questions.q: ___ nearly there yet?
questions.explanation: This is a yes/no question requiring subject-auxiliary inversion. 'Are we' correctly inverts the subject and auxiliary verb to form a question.

questions.q: England is ___ than Egypt.
questions.explanation: When comparing two countries, the comparative form 'more expensive' is required, not the superlative.

questions.q: I come from ___ small village near Paris.
questions.explanation: An indefinite article is needed before 'small village' because it is being mentioned for the first time (non-specific). 'A' is used before consonant sounds.

questions.q: If I take a big breath I can ___ 20 meters underwater.
questions.explanation: After the modal verb 'can', the bare infinitive (base form) is used: 'can swim'.

questions.q: Alice ___ a lovely meal for us at her house last Sunday.
questions.explanation: 'Last Sunday' indicates a completed past action, so the simple past tense 'cooked' is correct.

questions.q: I ___ to the cinema.
questions.explanation: Frequency adverbs like 'often' are placed before the main verb in affirmative sentences: 'I often go'.

questions.q: The store will ___ your groceries to your house.
questions.explanation: After the modal verb 'will', the bare infinitive (base form) is used: 'will deliver'.

questions.q: Ali ___ to go to bed early, so he didn't come to the party last night.
questions.explanation: The sentence is set in the past ('last night'), so the simple past tense 'wanted' is correct.

questions.q: Digital cameras are good ___ you don't need a film.
questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces a reason or cause. Not needing a film is the reason why digital cameras are good.
